These tutorials take you from zero to a working multimodal alignment,
introducing one concept at a time. They begin with hand-built timelines and
reach loading real data in the fourth notebook. Each notebook can be run
locally after installing the library with `pip install "timetoalign[tutorial]"`.

**Prerequisites:** Python 3.11+, basic familiarity with Jupyter notebooks.

## Tutorial Notebooks

::: {#tutorial-listing}
:::


## Topics at a Glance

The tutorials are designed to be followed in order, following a learning curve
from foundations through practical data work to the internals of the model:

### Foundations

- [Quickstart](tutorials/tut00_quickstart.ipynb) ---
  What the library is for, in five minutes: one section per tutorial that follows.
- [Timelines and Coordinates](tutorials/tut01_timelines_and_coordinates.ipynb) ---
  Coordinates, units, domains, the six timeline classes, and conversion maps.
- [Nesting and Timestamps](tutorials/tut02_nesting_and_timestamps.ipynb) ---
  Children, offsets, regions, segment lines, and the cross-section a timestamp gives you.
- [Events on a Timeline](tutorials/tut03_events.ipynb) ---
  Adding events, EventData, the shared filter vocabulary, and one timestamp per event.

### Working with Data

- [Loading Real Data](tutorials/tut04_loading_data.ipynb) ---
  The two-phase loader contract, EventStores, timeline ids, and what a loader builds for you.
- [Timeline Groups](tutorials/tut05_timeline_groups.ipynb) ---
  Commensurability, one shared start and end, exact linear conversion, timestamps from a group, and a child as a partial member.
- [Alignment Bundles and MatchClaims](tutorials/tut06_alignment_bundles.ipynb) ---
  Claims, claim types, MatchLines and WarpMaps, MatchStamps, and support policies.
- [Flow Control and Grids](tutorials/tut07_flow_and_grids.ipynb) ---
  Folded and unfolded time, FlowMaps, apply_flow, and beat grids.

### Under the Hood

- [The Data Model](tutorials/tut08_data_model.ipynb) ---
  Why PyArrow, the three layers, raw and semantic fields, blueprints, and Parquet metadata.
- [Pitch and Harmony across Formats](tutorials/tut09_pitch_and_harmony.ipynb) ---
  What each format knows about a note, and why the library refuses to invent the rest.
